frequency_question: How often do executive principals with jurisdiction over accrediting bodies follow through on revocation of recognition within a two-year policy window?
membership_rule: Includes formal administrative actions by federal cabinet-level departments to revoke or terminate the recognition of major institutional or professional accrediting agencies. Excludes routine renewals, voluntary relinquishments, or purely advisory warnings without final decertification orders.

cases.name: Department of Education termination of ACICS recognition (First instance)
Department of Education termination of ACICS recognition (Second instance / final confirmation after remand)

provenance_note: claims 60 cases from only 2 named (30.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 2 named termination events out of a total population of roughly 60 active national/regional/specialized accreditors evaluated across three decades.
known_gaps: Excludes minor specialized accreditors that surrendered recognition voluntarily under pressure prior to a formal final order.
skeleton: Total formal federal reviews of major national accreditors resulting in an initial or final withdrawal order by the Secretary of Education over a 30-year span.
multiplier: 2 confirmed termination orders across approximately 60 recognized accrediting bodies monitored over multiple renewal cycles yields a baseline activation frequency.
validity_reason: The statutory and regulatory framework governing federal recognition of accreditors remains stable across standard executive administration transitions, making historical agency-level friction rates applicable through the near term.
